original.description: Objective: The objective of the activity is to develop and test a thin optical aperture leveraging advances in integrated photonic technology to reduce the size andweight of space-based optical communication terminals.TargetedImprovements:Reduction of both size and weight of satellite laser communication terminals by 50%.Description: Optical communication terminal solutions with lower size and weight are required to serve the increasing role of small spacecraft for satellitecommercialisation by maximising the amountof payload space for mission-enabling processing or sensors. State-of-the-art optical communicationterminals are often too bulky and heavy for such small platforms and a leap in technology is required. This activity will seek innovative integrated photonicsolutions to replace the telescope subsystem of an optical communication terminal and eliminate as much as possible the need for free-space propagationinside the laser terminal. By doing so, it is expected to greatly reduce the size and inertial mass of the telescope subsystem, enabling for instance furtherreductions in steering assembly size, weight and power.This activity will design and prototype a photonic aperture (or flat telescope) that shall provide good beam quality (for coupling/emitting into/from singlemode waveguides such as single-mode fibres), shall be relatively large (at least several cm in diameter) or provide enough optical gain to enable convincingreplacement of conventional beam expansion and free-space propagation optics (traditional telescope assemblies) in space optical communicationterminals. A foundry-compatible fabrication process of the photonic aperture shall also provide a low-cost telescope alternative by eliminating the need forexpensive optics and assembly and alignment touch labour.The following tasks are envisioned:- Identify the potential solutions and latest innovations in integrated photonic able to replace conventional optical aperture assemblies in space-basedoptical communications for small platforms and/or use cases where accommodation of optical communication terminals is drastically constrained bytheir size and weight.- Develop a preliminary design and expected performance of the chosen solution.- Manufacture and test a prototype and evaluate the performance in a representative laboratory environment.Procurement Policy: C(1) = Activity restricted to non-prime contractors (incl. SMEs).  For additional information please go to:http://www.esa.int/About_Us/Business_with_ESA/Small_and_Medium_Sized_Enterprises/Opportunities_for_SMEs/Procurement_policy_on_fair_access_for_SMEs_-_the_C1-C4_Clauses

original.description: ESA operates one of the world's largest Earth Observation (EO) data archives, with data from missions dating back to the mid 1970s.Preserving these datatogether with the information and tools needed to interpret and use themis essential to analyse long-term environmental changes and support future decision-making. Within the EOF-EOS framework, long-term preservation of ESA's EO data holdings (Heritage Missions, Earth Explorers, Third Party Missions) and associated information and software is ensured through the Space Data Preservation System (SDPS), with assets located at ESRIN and external sites.Despite major progress, a significant volume of EO heritage data remains stored on legacy media at ESRIN and still requires transcription, recovery, and preservation in line with international standards. Beyond preservation and access, heritage data must be curated and improved to ensure continuity and comparability with newer missions. The generation of thematic collections and geographical datasets has further enhanced their usability and value.The Preservation Assets Operations and Maintenance (PAOM) Service will:Operate, maintain, and evolve Space Data Preservation System (SDPS) assets located at ESRIN;Manage the ESRIN EO Legacy Media Archive and Transcription Chains and perform legacy media transcription and data recovery;Generate thematic collections and geographical coverages using heritage data;Manage the ESRIN laboratory activities in support to transcription chains set-up and Philab Air Quality Platform activities, and manage and maintain the ESRIN AF Antenna;Support local visits at the Heritage Missions Walkthrough and Memorabilia Wall located at ESRIN and heritage missionsrelated outreach activities.

original.description: Objective: To derive a standard set of requirements for the ADHA (Advanced Data Handling Architecture) Security Module and implement a prototype form-factor equivalent ADHA module.Description: The ADHA (Advanced Data Handling Architecture) has been initiated through a collaboration between ESA, European satellite primes and data handling equipment suppliers. The initiative has resulted in the agreement on an architecture for data handling unit based on standard module functions. A standard module procurement flow has been defined, as well as a standardized backplane connector and electrical interfaces. This allows independent development of interoperable modules that can be connected together in ADHA units. More advanced security functions are expected to be required in future ESA missions. The modular format of the proposed solution will enable faster adoption, and verification of new security technologies, in different unit configurations. This activity aims to perform analysis work to derive a standardization of the security function within an ADHA module form-factor, to allow the development of ADHA-compliant security products, which can be utilized together with other existing ADHA products, such as ADHA OBC. When implemented in the ADHA 3U form factor, such units are of particular interest for use in mid-size satellite platforms as well (less than 500kg mass). For prototyping purposes, the target of this activity is an elegant breadboard (EBB) of the ADHA security module in 6U format, based on the security function requirements defined in this activity. The extended format will provide the required design margins for the prototyping and demonstration phase. The long-term goal, this technology development, is the adaptation of this security module to an ADHA 3U module form factor. This activity encompasses thefollowing tasks: - Analyse the use-cases for dedicated security modules in data handling systems, both for platform and payload - Derive the detailed generic requirements for ADHA Security Modules, including functions, performances, electrical and software interfaces, etc. and present the specifications for review of the ADHA consortia and industrial working group - Derive the architectural design of a prototype ADHA Security Module - Derive a prototype electrical and software design of an ADHA Security Module, as an EBB in ADHA 6U format. - Perform functional validation of the prototype and demonstrate a representative use-case for the ADHA Security Module - Derive a roadmap for bringing the derived design to an ADHA 3U security module EM/EQM/FM.

original.description: ObjectivesAssess the feasibility of using physics-based granular dynamics simulation to model the formation of cryovolcanic terrains on Enceladus and derive insights into surface compactness. Develop a proof-of-concept ML model for inferring snow/ice geophysicalproperties (e.g., density, snow water equivalent) by correlating terrestrial in-situ scientific data with satellite remote sensing observations. Initiate the adaptation of classical, optimization-based HDA frameworks to integrate AIderived geophysical safety maps, establishing a baseline for a future hybrid HDA architecture. Conduct an extensive performance and resource consumption benchmark of key AI and HDA software components on representative space-grade hardware, establishing the trade-space between algorithmic capability and on-board computational budgetDescriptionThe ESA Voyage 2050 L4 mission to Enceladus requires an autonomous landing in the South Polar Terrain to achieve its core astrobiological objectives. This environment presents unique challenges that transcend classical HDA capabilities. Landing hazardsare not only geometric (e.g., slopes, rocks), but also geophysical. Due to the unknown load-bearing capacity of cryovolcanic surface deposits, landing sites can appear perfectly flat and clear of hazards and yet be catastrophically unsafe. Classical existing Hazard Detection and Avoidance (HDA) frameworks targeting Moon and Mars, are highly mature for geometric hazard assessment but are not designed to infer subsurface geophysical properties from remote sensing data. This activity shall address this critical technology gap by investigating the integration of AI/ML-based geophysicalinference into a proven HDA decision-making architecture. Additionally, the severe power and computational constraints of a solar-powered missionto Saturn imposea hard limit on the complexity of on-board AI. It is currently unknown what level of "intelligence" is achievable within a realistic resource budget. This activity shall perform the foundational trade-off analysis required to inform mission designers of the necessary hardware and power provisions for a reliable and capable AI-augmented HDA system

original.description: Objective: To define and assess the feasibility of a digitally controlled, highly efficient and compact High-Power Amplifiers in L-band / C-band for PNT applications.Description: With the increased demand for navigation services, the number of signal componentstransmitted by a GNSS satellite has increased. Since constant envelope multiplexing schemes are not suitable (or inefficient) with ahigh number of signal components, modern GNSS systems generate signals with high PAPR (Peak to average Power Ratio). DC power efficiency is critical for high power amplifiers (HPA) transmitting signals with high PAPR. In the last decades several HPA architectureshave been investigated to solve this limitation. Among those, the category of polar transmitters such as Envelope Tracking (ET) andEnvelope Elimination and Restoration (EER) stand out for high efficiency and excellent thermal management of the transistors. Conversely, they showed major challenges such as high complexity and difficult implementation with wideband signals. Given the narrowbandnature of Position, Navigation and Timing (PNT) signals, polar transmitters are a good candidate for PNT applications. The challenge of analogue envelope reconstruction can be overcome by a digital modulator, leveraging recent advances in digital technologies. Atthe same time, evolution of PNT services is moving beyond L-band, targeting C-band or other frequency bands with larger bandwidths,where there is no example of dedicated HPAs for navigation. This activity will investigate amplifier design solutions to address high PAPR narrow band, as well as medium PAPR broadband signal configurations. The amplifiers will include digital predistortion, to achieve high-quality PNT signal performance, and compact designs to target advanced payload architectures. The selected designs willbe demonstrated through the development and testing of elegant breadboards (EBB) This activity encompasses the following tasks: - Definition of the operational scenarios and end-to-end user requirements associated. - Literature review, oriented at the latest developments in ET and polar transmitters in general, in analogue and in digital domain, as well as in broadband HPA solutions - Trade-off and down-selection of the most promising technologies based on the survey and preliminary high-level studies - Breadboards detailed design, and analysis and preparation of manufacturing plan and test plan - Breadboards manufacturing and test - Critical analysis of the results obtained and future roadmap.Procurement Policy: C(1) = Activity restricted to non-prime contractors (incl. SMEs).
